policies.description: Instance/query filter inputs reject more than InputValidator.MaxFiltersCount filters and any filter string longer than InputValidator.MaxFilterLength.

Filter field paths must satisfy InputValidator.ValidateFieldName: length limits, max dot depth, alphanumeric segments starting with a letter, and rejection of dangerous punctuation/control characters.

InstanceQueryValidator and SQL condition builders enforce InputValidator.MaxValueLength before SQL compilation. Each decoded scalar operand may contain at most 1000 UTF-16 code units (.NET string.Length), including every array element and each legacy comma-separated in/nin/between operand. Applies to instance columns and JSON attributes, including nested fields, logical groups and filter envelopes. HTTP queries reject violations with 400 and validation code filter.valueTooLong; GetInstancesTask returns a validation failure before local/remote dispatch, which can invoke the workflow error boundary. Includes objects retain their dedicated size/depth/property limits. Stored instance data is unaffected. The constant existed before this release, but the filter paths did not enforce it.

Includes-filter JSON payloads must be objects bounded by InputValidator MaxIncludesPayloadJsonLength, MaxIncludesPayloadNestingDepth, and MaxIncludesPayloadPropertyCount (including array element counts).

Arbitrary JSON strings are capped by InputValidator.ValidateJsonLength (same max as filters); JSONB column identifiers must pass InputValidator.ValidateSqlJsonColumnIdentifier (PostgreSQL-safe quoted identifiers).
ActorAuthorizationSpecification requires ExecutionActor.System for TriggerType.Automatic transitions.
ActorAuthorizationSpecification requires ExecutionActor.System for TriggerType.Scheduled transitions.
ActorAuthorizationSpecification rejects automatic transitions when TransitionExecutionContext.ChainDepth exceeds 50 (defense in depth alongside the pipeline).
TransitionAuthorizationManager evaluates transition RoleGrant lists: any matching DENY denies; otherwise any matching ALLOW permits; empty role grants allow all callers.

A caller with no roles cannot pass a role-bound DENY grant (a static role or a $role. reference): TransitionAuthorizationManager.IsUnprovableRoleBoundDeny refuses it in both RoleGrantEvaluator and EvaluateRolesStatic, on every surface and for every caller-role provider. Identity-bound denies (predefined roles, $user., $userBehalfOf.) keep their normal evaluation. This is what makes MorphIdmCallerRoleResolver resolving every failure (error status, timeout, transport, unparseable body, no act_sub/client_id) to an empty role set safe: an empty set can only narrow access, never widen it.

When an instance is present, TransitionAuthorizationManager resolves $InstanceStarter, $PreviousUser, $InstanceBehalfOfStarter, $PreviousBehalfOfUser against CreatedBy/CreatedByBehalfOf and last completed manual transition; dynamic grants use $.context.* paths compared to actor, subject, or caller role.

SchemaFieldFilterService applies master-schema x-masking after x-roles pruning on instance GET, instance list, the data function and sync start/transition attributes (IInstanceDataReadService), and on the Get* trigger tasks for the header set the task presents. x-masking.roles and x-encryption.roles are allow-only exemption lists resolved with IRoleGrantEvaluator.IsAnyRoleAllowed; role-resolution failure, an empty role set and unlisted roles keep the value transformed, and a role-less caller never satisfies a role-bound grant (static role or $role.). FieldMaskingDefinition rejects deny grants and co-occurrence with x-filterOperators, x-sortable or an active x-encryption at publish. x-encryption.type 'hash' is applied on write under a per-instance salt and takes no roles.

x-encryption.type 'encrypt': InstanceDataWriteService seals the declared string paths of InstancesData with AES-256-GCM under the instance's own key (AAD bound to scheme, instance and path) after validation; InstanceData.Data is the column as stored and is never decrypted in place (no plaintext member, no materialization interceptor), so no tracking state writes plaintext; decryption only through IInstanceDataProtector.UnprotectAsync (write funnel, read guard, script DecryptAsync of the instance's own path); content and DataHash are ignored after save and detached rows are attached Unchanged. DataHash of a row with tokens is keyed. Per-instance key and salt are generated by the runtime and stored in the flow schema's InstanceSecrets table (plaintext by decision: database security is owned by the DB team); they are cached in-process only, never in Redis, and never served on any API, log, span or cache. Allow-listed callers (x-encryption.roles) read plaintext on the data function and sync responses, all others the stored token; instance GET/list serve the stored token. A write carrying an undecryptable value forward is refused (Instance:100040) and reserved-prefix injection is rejected (Instance:100041). Queries on encrypted paths are refused. Scope: InstanceData only.
